summary: Phase 2 (messaging + mutual reviews + advanced filters + map) fully validated. Backend: 35/35 pytest tests passing (18 baseline + 17 new — conversations, messages, reviews lifecycle including rating recompute & duplicate guard, booking annotations 'reviewed'+'conversation_id', filters max_rate/min_rating/sort/distance/available). Frontend (Expo web, 375x667): client login -> Messages tab visible -> 3 conversations listed with testID conversation-* -> chat screen opens with chat-input + send-button -> message sent and visible. Bookings tab shows completed bookings with Message button + 'Avis publié' badge (already-reviewed). Category list /plombier opens FiltersModal with all chip groups (tarif, note, tri, dispo, près de moi), sort=rate_asc applied, toggle-view switches to ArtisanMap.web fallback showing 'Carte interactive disponible sur l'app mobile' + map-artisan-* items. Artisan detail shows 'Avis clients' reviews section.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warns: "shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow". (RN Web deprecation, non-blocking but should migrate to React Native 0.76+ recommended `boxShadow`).

action_items: Minor: FiltersModal rate/rating chip testIDs include the label string with special chars ('filter-rate-≤ 50€', 'filter-rating-4★+'). Functional but harder for E2E selectors. Recommend renaming to value-based testIDs like 'filter-rate-50' / 'filter-rating-4'.
Minor: replace deprecated React Native Web `shadow*` style props with `boxShadow` (or use Platform.select) to silence console warnings.

Optional: review modal flow couldn't be E2E-tested via UI because both existing 'completed' bookings for the seeded client already have reviews ('Avis publié' shown). Component code + testIDs (star-1..5, review-comment, submit-review-button) are correct and POST /api/reviews is fully covered by pytest. If you want an interactive review demo, create a new completed booking from artisan dashboard first.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~613 lines — still acceptable, but consider splitting into routers (auth, artisans, bookings, reviews, messaging) when adding payments.
Conversation auth check uses `403` for both 'not participant' AND 'conversation not found' — would be cleaner to return 404 when conv missing vs 403 when not participant. Not a bug, just clarity.
All endpoints consistently exclude `_id` (projection {_id:0}), uuid-based IDs, proper Pydantic validation. Good.
Subscription is still SIMULATED (no real Stripe). Confirmed mocked as expected (Phase 3 scope).
